source.title: Depth-Attention: Cross-Layer Value Mixing for Language Models
source.authors: Bo-Yi Zeng; Yi-Qing Hao; Zi-Tong Wang; Shi-Xiang Song; He Li; Fei Song; Yifan Liu; Zi-Wei He; Xinbing Wang; Zhou-Han Lin

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some tables are flattened and Figure 2's plotted values are not available as text.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports a parameter-size sweep of validation loss, which bears conceptually on loss scaling, but it does not reproduce the original scaling-law fitting method.
record.gate_note: Figure 2 reports validation-loss scaling trends for vanilla and Depth-Attention models at several sizes. Other reported results, including downstream scores, perplexity comparisons, efficiency measurements, and the looped-model result, do not test the claim versions about power-law loss scaling, extrapolation, compute-optimal allocation, architecture insensitivity, or downstream predictability. The paper cites Kaplan et al. for a compute-cost approximation, not as a test of the loss scaling law.
record.test_reason: This is an architecture paper. Figure 2 sweeps 360M–3B (under one order of magnitude) at a fixed 32B tokens, only to show Depth-Attention's loss stays below vanilla. It reports no exponents, no fit form or quality, no extrapolation check and no allocation analysis. The fitted trend is used as a tool, to estimate a parameter-equivalent gain for the method. Nothing in it bears on whether loss follows a power law (V1) or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also claim Depth-Attention 'improves the scaling behavior' of decoders, and use the fitted trend to estimate the parameter saving at 1.5B. They do not test the scaling law itself.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares a new cross-layer value-mixing architecture with vanilla models across sizes; it does not reproduce the original scaling-law fitting procedure.

fits_no_version.finding: A parameter-free change to the attention value path lowers loss at fixed parameter count: 500M loss 2.2348 to 2.2115; 1.5B perplexity 8.17 to 7.77; 3B perplexity 7.55 to 7.25.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-layer value mixing shifts the loss-versus-parameters curve downward by a constant-like offset from 360M to 3B.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The parameter sweep spans 360M to 3B and uses 32B training tokens; plotted loss values and numerical fit details are not reported in the text. The paper also states it validates only up to 3B parameters and 32B tokens.
record.rows_left_out: The paper excludes an earlier 160M setting from its final scaling analysis (Appendix C). No other results bearing directly on the tested loss-versus-parameter scaling version were left out.

untested.parts: Whether loss follows a power law at all: no fit form, exponent or fit quality is reported. The range is under one order of magnitude and the token count is fixed.
No small-run fit is evaluated against a larger run.
No depth or width comparison at a fixed parameter count.
No other modality or training regime is studied.
Downstream scores are reported, but not tested for predictability from scale or loss.

record.verdict_notes: The record's V1 limits_scope label should be dropped. It rested on cannot_determine rows and on untested parts, neither of which grounds a verdict. The scaling points mix Qwen-style (360M–710M) and Qwen3-style (1.5B, 3B) configs and use different learning rates. Kaplan et al. is cited only for the 6ND/2N compute approximation.

versions.untested_parts: The sweep varies parameter count while keeping the stated pretraining setup fixed; it does not vary training tokens or compute independently. It covers 360M to 3B, not several orders of magnitude, and does not report fitted power-law exponents or numerical validation-loss values.
No small-run fit is evaluated against the observed loss of a much larger run.
No fixed-compute-budget comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is reported.
The study does not compare depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
The study is about text pretraining; the looped-Transformer result is a single comparison, not a test of whether the same power-law form holds in another regime.
Downstream task scores are reported, but not as a test of predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
The study does not compare fitting choices or show that scaling curves bend away from a single power law.
